To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the stability indices of a linear time-invariant system are: a) invariant under feedback compensation, b) invariant under state-space transformation, and c) the only invariants of a linear time invariant system.
the stability indices of a linear time-invariant system provide the exact solution to the feedback stabilization and feedback control design problem.

(a) the stability indices of a linear system can be extracted from the structure of its minimal state-space realization; (b) the stability indices are invariant to all internally stable compensators; (c) the stability indices determine the structure of all possible compensators that can stabilize the system; (d) the stability indices characterize the structure of all internally stable compensating systems; and (e) the stability indices provide a basis for the exact characterization of the set of internally stable compensating controllers.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions: (1) What are the stability indices of a system, and how can they be computed?
the following questions: (1) How to determine the stability indices from the system matrices?
the following questions: What is the set of internally stabilizable dynamics for a given system?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
linear realization theory is a powerful tool for feedback control design.
Kalman’s realization theory provides a powerful and complete tool for the analysis and design of internally stable feedback control systems.
the theory of linear realization is the theory of linear feedback control.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have developed an exact algebraic characterization for the set of internally stable feedback compensators for a given linear time invariant plant, and we have derived a set of integer invariants that permit an efficient computation of the stability indices.
the stability indices of a system are the key invariants for the design of internally stable linear feedback control.
the stability indices of a given system are a complete invariant for the set of all stabilizable dynamics assignments.
The main takeaway from our work is that
this characterization can be obtained by a systematic and efficient algorithm.
this characterization can be extended to the case of systems with a single unstable pole.

this characterization is possible even if one is interested in a specific class of compensators—e.g., those with finite-dimensional state space, or those with a specific number of inputs and/or outputs.
